title: Design: LRU Cache (O(1))
hints: O(1) needs a dictionary for lookup plus a doubly linked list for recency.
Use sentinel head and tail nodes; move a node to the front on each access and evict `tail.prev` when over capacity.
`unlink(n); pushFront(n)` on hits; on overflow: `let lru = tail.prev!; unlink(lru); map[lru.key] = nil`.
jsBridge: An O(1) LRU needs a dictionary plus a doubly linked list. JS's `Map` preserves insertion order, so JS devs cheat with delete-then-set. Swift's `Dictionary` is unordered, so you build the list yourself, with `weak`/`unowned` back-links.

compass.q: The JS `Map` delete-and-reinsert trick gives LRU for free. Why doesn't it work in Swift?
Hand-rolled LRU vs `NSCache` (auto-evicts under memory pressure): which for images?
Doubly linked nodes create reference cycles. How do you avoid leaking them?
Should an LRU be an actor if multiple image loads hit it concurrently?
